calibration invariants: I1 |Gamma_cal(0)-1| = 0.0e+00; I2 order preserved on 1.0000; I3 1/kappa gradient = 0.0e+00; I4 FD agreement 6.5e-08; I5 11085 non-positive Gamma_raw all flagged (paper fallback applied); I6 kappa=2 changes Gamma by up to 4.044
Eq.(26) on an explicit map f = Aq + b: relative error 9.2e-08 (kappa=1) and 9.2e-08 (kappa=2, including the 1/kappa factor)

single-point evaluation 403 us (3000-BV sparse model would be ~5x less); batched evaluation 764 us/point over 24892 points. Python/NumPy only: the 2 ms real-time budget is met in order of magnitude, but the paper's C implementation is not reproduced

feeding Gamma_raw into log(Gamma-1) without calibration: 11085 points lie outside the domain and become NaN unless the paper's large-negative fallback (-1000) is applied -- counted, never silently propagated
permuting the 36 unnamed columns moves the constant triples (detected by P7.1's column check) and drops the y_est agreement from 1.0000 to 0.5547

reading the CPSP penalty '-g 3.3' as the RBF width (sigma = 3.3) instead of converting it (sigma = 1/sqrt(2g) = 0.38925) drops the y_est agreement from 1.0000 to 0.5670.  Note the measured caveat: the two *published* sigmas differ by only 0.28% and score 0.9992 when swapped, so they are numerically interchangeable -- the model/sigma pairing is enforced for provenance, not for accuracy
kappa=2 with the 1/kappa factor omitted leaves a gradient error of 13.717, i.e. I3 fails by a factor of two
asserting Gamma_cal == Gamma_raw at kappa=2 is false by up to 4.044: the calibration map is not the identity once kappa != 1
all-zero feature vector gives a finite Gamma_raw = 3.5749 (no division by zero in the kernel path)
